decisions.reason: As a niche agricultural crate with only limited website prominence and four seasons of likely market learning, its upside now looks too narrow to justify keeping the option open.

A foldable large container fits the firm’s core reusable logistics portfolio, had strong initial prominence, and likely shares tooling and customers with the established business, so the option remains attractive.
A stackable plastic crate is a standard adjacent offer whose carrying cost is likely low and whose value can still be realized across multiple customer segments, favoring retention.
The rackable pallet sits close to the firm’s core pallet business and can complement existing accounts, so despite only modest visibility it is still worth keeping on the market.

The spill-retention pallet appears to be a more specialized option whose reduced prominence suggests limited traction, and by 2022 uncertainty should be resolved enough to reallocate resources elsewhere.

A plastic pallet with load retainers is a practical extension of the core pallet range, and the firm can keep this option open at relatively low incremental cost while serving logistics customers with specific securing needs.
